```json
{"claims":[{"claim_text":"The legal immigration framework was last updated in 1990 and does not reflect the needs of the United States in the 21st century.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Many immigrants are forced to wait years, and often decades, to immigrate lawfully to the United States.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"A robust immigration system with accessible lawful pathways and penalties for illegal immigration alleviates pressure at the border and upholds values.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The U.S. Citizenship Act would permanently increase family-sponsored and employment-based immigration.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The bipartisan border legislation would increase the number of immigrant visas that are available by 250,000 over 5 years.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"President Biden has used his authority to provide orderly, legal immigration pathways for those fleeing violence, and decrease the number of illegal border crossings.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[4]},{"claim_text":"The Biden-Harris Administration established a humanitarian parole process for Cubans, Haitians, Nicaraguans, and Venezuelans (CHNV), which allows people from these four countries who have a sponsor in the U.S. and who pass a background check to come to the U.S. for a period of two years to live and work lawfully.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[4]},{"claim_text":"Border encounters from Cubans, Haitians, Nicaraguans, and Venezuelans decreased by 89 percent in the first six months after CHNV was put in place, incentivizing migrants to stay in place, rather than make the dangerous journey to the southwest border.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[4]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
